# Markdown to Confluence

Source: https://github.com/7nohe/confluence-md/blob/main/README.md

# Markdown to Confluence

Convert Markdown (GFM) to Confluence Cloud storage format and update an existing page.

Available as both a **GitHub Action** and a **CLI tool**.

## Features
- GFM conversion with tables, strikethrough, task list text fallback
- Mermaid code fences to Confluence mermaid macro
- Local image uploads or external image URLs
- Skip update when content is unchanged
- Dry run mode to inspect generated storage XML
- Directory sync for multiple Markdown files

## Requirements
- Confluence Cloud site
- API token with permission to update the target page
- Mermaid macro enabled in Confluence if you use Mermaid fences

## Usage

### CLI

Install and run with npx:

```bash
# Set API token as environment variable (required)
export CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN="your-api-token"

# Basic usage
npx @7nohe/confluence-md docs/page.md \
  --url https://example.atlassian.net \
  --email you@example.com

# With page ID specified
npx @7nohe/confluence-md docs/page.md \
  --url https://example.atlassian.net \
  --email you@example.com \
  --page-id 123456

# Dry run (preview without updating)
npx @7nohe/confluence-md docs/page.md --dry-run

# JSON output for scripting
npx @7nohe/confluence-md docs/page.md --json

# Directory sync (page IDs must be defined in frontmatter)
npx @7nohe/confluence-md docs/ \
  --url https://example.atlassian.net \
  --email you@example.com

# Short alias
cfmd docs/page.md --dry-run
```

#### CLI Options

```
-u, --url <url>            Confluence base URL (or CONFLUENCE_BASE_URL env)
-e, --email <email>        Confluence account email (or CONFLUENCE_EMAIL env)
-p, --page-id <id>         Confluence page ID (or use frontmatter)
--title <title>            Override page title
--attachments-base <path>  Base directory for resolving image paths
--image-mode <mode>        Image handling: upload or external (default: upload)
--download-remote-images   Download remote images as attachments
--no-skip-unchanged        Update even if content unchanged
--dry-run                  Preview without updating Confluence
--json                     Output results as JSON
-v, --verbose              Enable verbose output
-c, --config <path>        Path to config file
```

#### Config File

Create `.confluence.yml` in your project root:

```yaml
confluence_base_url: https://example.atlassian.net
email: you@example.com
frontmatter_page_id_key: confluence_page_id
image_mode: upload
skip_if_unchanged: true
```

Note: API token must be set via `CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN` environment variable for security.

#### Directory Sync

You can pass a directory to `source` in both CLI and GitHub Action. The tool scans the directory recursively and syncs every `*.md` file in order.

Each Markdown file must define its own page ID in frontmatter:

```markdown
---
confluence_page_id: 123456
---

# Page title
```

When `source` is a directory:

- `page_id` is ignored to prevent accidental overwrites
- `attachments_base` defaults to each file's own directory when not explicitly set
- CLI `--json` returns aggregate results and per-file details

### GitHub Action

```yaml
name: Publish docs
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: 7nohe/confluence-md@v0.1.5
        with:
          confluence_base_url: https://example.atlassian.net
          email: you@example.com
          api_token: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN }}
          source: docs/
```

### Frontmatter page ID

```markdown
---
confluence_page_id: 123456
title: My Confluence Page
---

# Page title
```

You can also pass `page_id` directly as an input for single-file syncs.
If frontmatter includes `title`, it is used as the Confluence page title. In single-file mode,
`title_override` still takes precedence.

## GitHub Action Inputs

| Name | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| confluence_base_url | yes | - | Confluence base URL (e.g. https://example.atlassian.net) |
| page_id | no | - | Confluence page ID (fallback if frontmatter missing in single-file mode) |
| email | yes | - | Confluence account email |
| api_token | yes | - | Confluence API token |
| source | yes | - | Markdown file or directory path |
| attachments_base | no | dir(source) | Base directory for resolving relative image paths |
| title_override | no | - | Override page title |
| frontmatter_page_id_key | no | confluence_page_id | Frontmatter key used to extract the page ID |
| image_mode | no | upload | Image handling mode: upload or external |
| download_remote_images | no | false | Download remote images and upload as attachments |
| mermaid_macro | no | mermaid | Macro name emitted for mermaid code fences (match your Confluence Mermaid app) |
| skip_if_unchanged | no | true | Skip update when storage output is identical |
| dry_run | no | false | Build output but do not update Confluence |
| notify_watchers | no | false | Accepted but currently ignored |
| user_agent | no | confluence-md | HTTP user agent |

## GitHub Action Outputs

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| page_url | URL of the updated Confluence page |
| page_id | ID of the updated Confluence page |
| version | New version number of the page |
| updated | Whether the page was actually updated (true or false) |
| attachments_uploaded | Number of attachments uploaded |
| content_hash | Hash of the generated storage content |
| total_files | Total number of Markdown files processed in directory mode |
| succeeded_files | Number of files processed successfully in directory mode |
| failed_files | Number of files that failed in directory mode |
| updated_files | Number of files updated in directory mode |
| attachments_uploaded_total | Total attachments uploaded in directory mode |
| results_json | JSON array of per-file results in directory mode |
| failures_json | JSON array of per-file failures in directory mode |

Single-file outputs (`page_url`, `page_id`, `version`, `updated`, `attachments_uploaded`, `content_hash`) are only populated for single-file runs. Directory runs use the aggregate outputs above.

## Image handling
- Local images are resolved relative to `attachments_base`.
- Remote images use `ri:url` when `image_mode=external`.
- If `download_remote_images=true`, remote images are downloaded and uploaded as attachments.
- In directory mode without `attachments_base`, local images are resolved relative to each Markdown file.

## Mermaid

Confluence Cloud has no built-in Mermaid macro, so rendering relies on a Mermaid
app installed in your site. ` ```mermaid ` code fences are converted to
`<ac:structured-macro ac:name="...">` with the diagram source as the macro body.

Because each Mermaid app uses a different macro name, set `mermaid_macro` to match
the app installed in your site (for example `mermaid-cloud`). The default is
`mermaid`. If no matching Mermaid app is installed, the diagram renders as an
unknown macro — in that case, pre-render the diagram to an image and reference it
as a normal Markdown image instead.

## Limitations
- Confluence Cloud only (no Server or Data Center support).
- Each Markdown file maps to a single Confluence page. Directory mode syncs multiple files sequentially.
- Raw HTML in Markdown is stripped for safety.
- For line breaks inside table cells, use `<br>` or `<br/>`. Literal newlines inside GFM table cells are not supported and may be parsed as separate rows.

## Versioning
This project follows Semantic Versioning. See `CHANGELOG.md` for release notes.

## License
MIT. See `LICENSE`.

---

# AGENTS.md

Source: https://github.com/7nohe/confluence-md/blob/main/AGENTS.md

# AGENTS.md

This file provides guidance to Codex (Codex.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

A GitHub Action and CLI tool that converts Markdown (GFM) files to Confluence Cloud storage format and updates Confluence pages. Available as both `npx @7nohe/confluence-md` (or `cfmd` / `confluence-md`) command and GitHub Action. Uses `@actions/http-client` for HTTP operations and `unified`/`remark` for Markdown parsing.

## Commands

```bash
# Build (bundles Action to dist/, CLI to dist/cli/)
npm run build

# Run tests
npm test

# Run single test file
npx vitest run tests/converter.test.ts

# Run tests in watch mode
npm run test:watch

# Lint & Format (Biome)
npm run check          # Check only
npm run check:fix      # Auto-fix

# Type checking
npm run typecheck

# Run all CI checks locally
npm run ci

# Test CLI locally
export CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN="your-token"
node dist/cli/index.js docs/page.md --url https://example.atlassian.net --email you@example.com --dry-run

# Test with act (requires Docker)
act push                                                    # Full CI
act -j test-action -W .github/workflows/test-action.yml     # Test action
```

See [DEVELOPMENT.md](./DEVELOPMENT.md) for details.

## Architecture

### Entry Points
- `src/main.ts` - GitHub Action entry point
- `src/cli.ts` - CLI entry point (Commander.js)

### Execution Flow
1. **Input handling** (`src/inputs.ts`) - Reads inputs from Action or CLI, validates, normalizes base URL
2. **Frontmatter extraction** (`src/frontmatter.ts`) - Extracts YAML frontmatter using `gray-matter`, gets page ID
3. **Markdown conversion** (`src/converter/`) - Parses GFM with `remark-parse`/`remark-gfm`, converts AST to Confluence storage XML
4. **Confluence API** (`src/confluence/`) - Manages page read/update and attachment uploads
5. **Core orchestration** (`src/core.ts`) - Shared business logic for both Action and CLI

### Shared Infrastructure
- `src/logger.ts` - Logger abstraction (Actions logger vs console logger vs silent)
- `src/core.ts` - Common conversion/update logic used by both entry points

### Converter Module (`src/converter/`)
- `index.ts` - Entry point, creates `unified` processor pipeline, tracks image references
- `nodes.ts` - Recursive AST node converters (headings, lists, tables, code blocks, images, etc.)
- `xml.ts` - XML utilities: escaping, CDATA wrapping, element/macro creation

### Confluence Module (`src/confluence/`)
- `client.ts` - HTTP client wrapper with Basic auth, handles JSON and multipart requests
- `pages.ts` - Page read (v2 API) and update operations
- `attachments.ts` - Attachment upload (v1 API with multipart/form-data), image downloading

### Key Conversion Rules
- Code fences with `mermaid` language produce `<ac:structured-macro ac:name="...">`; the macro name is configurable via the `mermaid_macro` input (default `mermaid`) to match the installed Confluence Mermaid app
- Other code fences produce `<ac:structured-macro ac:name="code">` with language parameter
- Local images become `<ac:image><ri:attachment ri:filename="..."/></ac:image>`
- Remote images use `<ri:url ri:value="..."/>` (or download if `download_remote_images` is enabled)
- Task lists render as `[ ]`/`[x]` text (no macro support)
- HTML blocks are stripped for security

### Image Handling
- Images are tracked in `ConversionContext.images` during conversion
- Collision handling: duplicate basenames get `_1`, `_2` suffixes
- Path traversal protection in `attachmentsBase` resolution

## Testing

Tests are in `tests/` using Vitest. Main test file `converter.test.ts` covers:
- XML utilities (escaping, CDATA, element creation)
- Markdown conversion (headings, formatting, lists, code blocks, tables, images)
- Frontmatter extraction

Run a specific test by name:
```bash
npx vitest run -t "should convert h1"
```

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

A GitHub Action and CLI tool that converts Markdown (GFM) files to Confluence Cloud storage format and updates Confluence pages. Available as both `npx confluence-md` (or `cfmd`) command and GitHub Action. Uses `@actions/http-client` for HTTP operations and `unified`/`remark` for Markdown parsing.

## Commands

```bash
# Build (bundles Action to dist/, CLI to dist/cli/)
npm run build

# Run tests
npm test

# Run single test file
npx vitest run tests/converter.test.ts

# Run tests in watch mode
npm run test:watch

# Lint & Format (Biome)
npm run check          # Check only
npm run check:fix      # Auto-fix

# Type checking
npm run typecheck

# Run all CI checks locally
npm run ci

# Test CLI locally
export CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN="your-token"
node dist/cli/index.js docs/page.md --url https://example.atlassian.net --email you@example.com --dry-run

# Test with act (requires Docker)
act push                                                    # Full CI
act -j test-action -W .github/workflows/test-action.yml     # Test action
```

See [DEVELOPMENT.md](./DEVELOPMENT.md) for details.

## Architecture

### Entry Points
- `src/main.ts` - GitHub Action entry point
- `src/cli.ts` - CLI entry point (Commander.js)

### Execution Flow
1. **Input handling** (`src/inputs.ts`) - Reads inputs from Action or CLI, validates, normalizes base URL
2. **Frontmatter extraction** (`src/frontmatter.ts`) - Extracts YAML frontmatter using `gray-matter`, gets page ID
3. **Markdown conversion** (`src/converter/`) - Parses GFM with `remark-parse`/`remark-gfm`, converts AST to Confluence storage XML
4. **Confluence API** (`src/confluence/`) - Manages page read/update and attachment uploads
5. **Core orchestration** (`src/core.ts`) - Shared business logic for both Action and CLI

### Shared Infrastructure
- `src/logger.ts` - Logger abstraction (Actions logger vs console logger vs silent)
- `src/core.ts` - Common conversion/update logic used by both entry points

### Converter Module (`src/converter/`)
- `index.ts` - Entry point, creates `unified` processor pipeline, tracks image references
- `nodes.ts` - Recursive AST node converters (headings, lists, tables, code blocks, images, etc.)
- `xml.ts` - XML utilities: escaping, CDATA wrapping, element/macro creation

### Confluence Module (`src/confluence/`)
- `client.ts` - HTTP client wrapper with Basic auth, handles JSON and multipart requests
- `pages.ts` - Page read (v2 API) and update operations
- `attachments.ts` - Attachment upload (v1 API with multipart/form-data), image downloading

### Key Conversion Rules
- Code fences with `mermaid` language produce `<ac:structured-macro ac:name="...">`; the macro name is configurable via the `mermaid_macro` input (default `mermaid`) to match the installed Confluence Mermaid app
- Other code fences produce `<ac:structured-macro ac:name="code">` with language parameter
- Local images become `<ac:image><ri:attachment ri:filename="..."/></ac:image>`
- Remote images use `<ri:url ri:value="..."/>` (or download if `download_remote_images` is enabled)
- Task lists render as `[ ]`/`[x]` text (no macro support)
- HTML blocks are stripped for security

### Image Handling
- Images are tracked in `ConversionContext.images` during conversion
- Collision handling: duplicate basenames get `_1`, `_2` suffixes
- Path traversal protection in `attachmentsBase` resolution

## Testing

Tests are in `tests/` using Vitest. Main test file `converter.test.ts` covers:
- XML utilities (escaping, CDATA, element creation)
- Markdown conversion (headings, formatting, lists, code blocks, tables, images)
- Frontmatter extraction

Run a specific test by name:
```bash
npx vitest run -t "should convert h1"
```

# Contributing

Source: https://github.com/7nohe/confluence-md/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

# Contributing

Thanks for helping improve confluence-md.

## Prerequisites
- Node.js 20+
- npm

## Setup
```bash
npm install
```

## Development
```bash
npm run test
npm run check
npm run typecheck
npm run build
```

## Notes
- This repository commits `dist/` outputs because GitHub Actions run from the bundled file.
- When you change `src/`, run `npm run build` to refresh `dist/`.
- Please include or update tests when changing conversion logic.

## Reporting issues
Include steps to reproduce, expected behavior, and logs when possible.

# Development Guide

Source: https://github.com/7nohe/confluence-md/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT.md

# Development Guide

This document explains how to develop and test confluence-md locally.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 24+ (the Action runs on the `node24` runtime)
- Docker Desktop
- [act](https://github.com/nektos/act) (for running GitHub Actions locally)

### Installing act (macOS)

```bash
brew install act
```

## Setup

```bash
# Install dependencies
npm install
```

## Development Commands

### Build

```bash
# Build both GitHub Action and CLI
npm run build

# GitHub Action only
npm run build:action

# CLI only
npm run build:cli
```

The Action bundle (`dist/index.js` and its runtime companions) is committed so
that `uses: 7nohe/confluence-md@vX` resolves a ready-to-run build at the release
tag. You do **not** build it by hand and you do **not** touch it in feature
PRs — the release workflow rebuilds it automatically and commits it **into the
release PR**, so the released commit always carries an up-to-date bundle while
your own pull requests stay free of `dist/` churn. (The CLI build, `dist/cli/`,
and type declarations are not committed; they are built on demand and at npm
publish time.)

### Test

```bash
# Run tests
npm test

# Watch mode
npm run test:watch

# Specific test file
npx vitest run tests/converter.test.ts

# Specific test name
npx vitest run -t "should convert h1"
```

### Lint & Format (Biome)

```bash
# Check only
npm run check

# Auto-fix
npm run check:fix

# Lint only
npm run lint
npm run lint:fix

# Format only
npm run format
npm run format:fix
```

### Type Check

```bash
npm run typecheck
```

### Run All CI Checks

```bash
# Runs Biome → TypeCheck → Test → Build sequentially
npm run ci
```

## Running GitHub Actions Locally with act

### Configuration

The `.actrc` file in the project root contains act settings:

```
--container-architecture linux/amd64
-P ubuntu-latest=catthehacker/ubuntu:act-latest
```

### List Available Workflows

```bash
act --list
```

### Run CI Workflow

```bash
# Run all jobs
act push

# Run specific job
act -j lint       # Biome check
act -j typecheck  # Type check
act -j test       # Tests
act -j build      # Build
```

### Test the Action Itself

You can verify the action works using dry-run mode (no Confluence API calls):

```bash
act -j test-action -W .github/workflows/test-action.yml
```

Test files:
- `test-fixtures/sample.md` - Sample Markdown file
- `.github/workflows/test-action.yml` - Test workflow

### Troubleshooting

#### Docker Disk Space Issues

```bash
docker system prune -af --volumes
```

#### act is Slow or Hanging

The workflow is configured without caching. If it's still slow, try restarting Docker.

#### Issues on M1/M2 Mac

The `.actrc` specifies `linux/amd64` architecture. If problems persist:

```bash
act push --container-architecture linux/amd64 -P ubuntu-latest=catthehacker/ubuntu:act-latest
```

## Project Structure

```
src/
├── main.ts           # GitHub Action entry point
├── cli.ts            # CLI entry point
├── core.ts           # Shared logic
├── inputs.ts         # Input parameter handling
├── frontmatter.ts    # YAML frontmatter parsing
├── logger.ts         # Logging abstraction
├── types.ts          # Type definitions
├── images.ts         # Image processing
├── converter/        # Markdown → Confluence conversion
│   ├── index.ts      # Conversion pipeline
│   ├── nodes.ts      # AST node converters
│   └── xml.ts        # XML utilities
└── confluence/       # Confluence API
    ├── client.ts     # HTTP client
    ├── pages.ts      # Page operations
    └── attachments.ts # Attachment operations

tests/                # Test files
test-fixtures/        # Test data
dist/index.js         # Action bundle (committed; refreshed by the release workflow)
```

## Commit Convention

This project uses [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) for automated releases.

### Format

```
<type>[optional scope]: <description>

[optional body]

[optional footer(s)]
```

### Types

| Type | Description | Version Bump |
|------|-------------|--------------|
| `feat` | New feature | Minor (0.x.0) |
| `fix` | Bug fix | Patch (0.0.x) |
| `perf` | Performance improvement | Patch |
| `docs` | Documentation only | None |
| `style` | Code style (formatting, etc.) | None |
| `refactor` | Code refactoring | None |
| `test` | Adding/updating tests | None |
| `chore` | Maintenance tasks | None |
| `ci` | CI/CD changes | None |

### Breaking Changes

For breaking changes, add `!` after the type or include `BREAKING CHANGE:` in the footer:

```bash
feat!: change API response format

# or

feat: change API response format

BREAKING CHANGE: The response format has changed from XML to JSON.
```

Breaking changes trigger a major version bump (x.0.0).

### Examples

```bash
# Feature
git commit -m "feat: add support for nested lists"

# Bug fix
git commit -m "fix: escape special characters in code blocks"

# Documentation
git commit -m "docs: update installation instructions"

# Breaking change
git commit -m "feat!: require Node.js 20+"
```

## Release Process

Releases are automated using [release-please](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please).

### How It Works

1. Push commits with Conventional Commits format to `main`/`master`
2. release-please automatically creates/updates a Release PR
3. The PR accumulates changes and updates:
   - `package.json` version
   - `CHANGELOG.md`
   - the rebuilt Action bundle (`dist/`), committed into the release PR by CI
4. Merge the Release PR to publish:
   - GitHub Release and version tag (e.g., `v1.2.3`) are created on the
     release commit, which already carries the up-to-date bundle
   - Major version tag (e.g., `v1`) is moved to that commit
   - The package is published to npm

### Manual Verification (Optional)

Before merging a Release PR:

1. `npm run ci` passes
2. `act push` succeeds
3. `act -j test-action -W .github/workflows/test-action.yml` succeeds

# Documentation Site

Source: https://github.com/7nohe/confluence-md/blob/main/docs/README.md

# Documentation Site

This directory contains the documentation site for confluence-md, built with [Starlight](https://starlight.astro.build/) (Astro).

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 20+
- npm

## Getting Started

```bash
# Install dependencies
npm install

# Start development server
npm run dev
```

The site will be available at http://localhost:4321

## Commands

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `npm run dev` | Start development server |
| `npm run build` | Build for production (output: `dist/`) |
| `npm run preview` | Preview production build locally |

## Directory Structure

```
docs/
├── astro.config.mjs          # Starlight configuration
├── package.json
├── tsconfig.json
├── public/
│   └── favicon.svg
└── src/
    ├── content.config.ts     # Content collection config
    └── content/
        └── docs/
            ├── index.mdx                 # English home (splash page)
            ├── getting-started/          # Getting Started section
            │   ├── installation.mdx
            │   └── quick-start.mdx
            ├── guides/                   # Guides section
            │   ├── basic-usage.mdx
            │   ├── frontmatter.mdx
            │   ├── images.mdx
            │   └── mermaid.mdx
            ├── reference/                # Reference section
            │   ├── inputs.mdx
            │   ├── outputs.mdx
            │   └── conversion-rules.mdx
            ├── development/              # Development section
            │   ├── architecture.mdx
            │   └── contributing.mdx
            └── ja/                       # Japanese translations
                └── ...                   # (same structure as above)
```

## Adding New Pages

1. Create a new `.mdx` file in the appropriate directory under `src/content/docs/`
2. Add frontmatter with at least `title` and `description`:

```mdx
---
title: My New Page
description: A brief description of this page.
---

# Content goes here
```

3. The page will automatically appear in the sidebar if using `autogenerate`

## Internationalization (i18n)

The site supports English (default) and Japanese.

### Adding translations

1. Create the same file path under `src/content/docs/ja/`
2. Translate the content while keeping the same frontmatter structure

### Sidebar translations

Sidebar labels are configured in `astro.config.mjs`:

```javascript
sidebar: [
  {
    label: 'Getting Started',
    translations: { ja: 'はじめに' },
    autogenerate: { directory: 'getting-started' },
  },
]
```

## Configuration

Main configuration is in `astro.config.mjs`:

- `title` - Site title
- `locales` - Language configuration
- `social` - Social links in header
- `sidebar` - Navigation structure

See [Starlight Configuration Reference](https://starlight.astro.build/reference/configuration/) for all options.

## Deployment

Build the site:

```bash
npm run build
```

The static output will be in the `dist/` directory, ready to deploy to any static hosting service (GitHub Pages, Netlify, Vercel, etc.).

# architecture.mdx

Source: https://github.com/7nohe/confluence-md/blob/main/docs/src/content/docs/development/architecture.mdx

title: Architecture
description: Technical overview of the project structure and execution flow.

## Project Structure

```
confluence-md/
├── src/
│   ├── main.ts              # Entry point, orchestrates the flow
│   ├── types.ts             # TypeScript interfaces
│   ├── inputs.ts            # GitHub Action input handling
│   ├── frontmatter.ts       # YAML frontmatter extraction
│   ├── images.ts            # Image path utilities
│   ├── converter/
│   │   ├── index.ts         # Unified processor pipeline
│   │   ├── nodes.ts         # AST node converters
│   │   └── xml.ts           # XML utilities
│   └── confluence/
│       ├── client.ts        # HTTP client wrapper
│       ├── pages.ts         # Page API operations
│       └── attachments.ts   # Attachment handling
├── tests/                   # Vitest test suites
├── dist/                    # Bundled output (ncc)
└── action.yml               # GitHub Action metadata
```

## Execution Flow

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Read Inputs] --> B[Read Markdown File]
    B --> C[Extract Frontmatter]
    C --> D[Parse Markdown to AST]
    D --> E[Convert AST to Confluence XML]
    E --> F[Compute Content Hash]
    F --> G{Dry Run?}
    G -->|Yes| H[Output Results]
    G -->|No| I[Fetch Current Page]
    I --> J{Content Changed?}
    J -->|No| H
    J -->|Yes| K[Upload Attachments]
    K --> L[Update Page]
    L --> H
```

## Key Modules

### Input Handling (`src/inputs.ts`)

Reads and validates GitHub Action inputs:
- Normalizes the Confluence base URL (removes trailing slashes)
- Sets default values for optional inputs
- Validates required inputs are present

### Frontmatter (`src/frontmatter.ts`)

Uses `gray-matter` to extract YAML frontmatter:
- Parses the frontmatter block
- Extracts the page ID using the configured key
- Returns both metadata and content body

### Converter (`src/converter/`)

#### `index.ts`
Creates the unified processing pipeline:
```
remark-parse → remark-gfm → custom converter → Confluence XML
```

Tracks images found during conversion for later upload.

#### `nodes.ts`
Recursive AST node converters handling:
- Block elements (paragraphs, headings, lists, tables)
- Inline elements (bold, italic, code, links)
- Special elements (code blocks, images, Mermaid)

#### `xml.ts`
XML utilities:
- `escapeXml()` - Escape special characters
- `cdata()` - Wrap content in CDATA sections
- `el()` - Create XML elements
- `macro()` - Create Confluence macro elements

### Confluence Client (`src/confluence/`)

#### `client.ts`
HTTP client wrapper using `@actions/http-client`:
- Basic authentication (email:token)
- JSON request/response handling
- Multipart form data for attachments

#### `pages.ts`
Page operations using Confluence v2 API:
- `getPage()` - Fetch page with storage body
- `updatePage()` - Update page content and version

#### `attachments.ts`
Attachment handling using Confluence v1 API:
- `uploadAttachment()` - Upload file as attachment
- `downloadImage()` - Download remote images

## API Versions

The action uses different Confluence API versions:

| API | Version | Endpoint Pattern |
|-----|---------|------------------|
| Pages | v2 | `/wiki/api/v2/pages/{id}` |
| Attachments | v1 | `/wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/child/attachment` |

The v2 API is used for pages because it provides cleaner JSON responses. The v1 API is used for attachments because attachment upload isn't available in v2.

## Content Hashing

To enable `skip_if_unchanged`, the action:
1. Computes SHA256 hash of the generated storage format
2. Truncates to first 16 characters
3. Compares with hash stored in page properties (if available)
4. Skips update if hashes match

## Build Process

The project uses `@vercel/ncc` to bundle all dependencies into a single file:

```bash
npm run build  # Outputs to dist/index.js
```

This creates a self-contained bundle that doesn't require `node_modules` at runtime.

# Clone the repository

Source: https://github.com/7nohe/confluence-md/blob/main/docs/src/content/docs/development/contributing.mdx

title: Contributing
description: How to contribute to the Confluence MD project.

## Development Setup

### Prerequisites

- Node.js 20 or higher
- npm

### Getting Started

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/daiki/confluence-md.git
cd confluence-md

# Install dependencies
npm install
```

## Available Commands

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `npm run build` | Bundle with ncc to `dist/index.js` |
| `npm test` | Run full test suite |
| `npm run test:watch` | Run tests in watch mode |
| `npm run typecheck` | TypeScript type checking |
| `npm run check` | Biome linting |
| `npm run format` | Format code with Biome |
| `npm run ci` | Run all checks (lint, typecheck, test, build) |

## Running Tests

```bash
# Run all tests
npm test

# Run a specific test file
npx vitest run tests/converter.test.ts

# Run tests matching a pattern
npx vitest run -t "should convert h1"

# Watch mode for development
npm run test:watch
```

## Project Structure

```
src/
├── main.ts           # Entry point
├── types.ts          # TypeScript interfaces
├── inputs.ts         # Input handling
├── frontmatter.ts    # Frontmatter extraction
├── images.ts         # Image utilities
├── converter/        # Markdown → Confluence conversion
│   ├── index.ts
│   ├── nodes.ts
│   └── xml.ts
└── confluence/       # Confluence API client
    ├── client.ts
    ├── pages.ts
    └── attachments.ts
```

## Making Changes

### 1. Create a Branch

```bash
git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name
```

### 2. Make Your Changes

- Follow existing code style
- Add tests for new functionality
- Update documentation if needed

### 3. Run Checks

```bash
npm run ci
```

This runs:
- Linting with Biome
- Type checking
- Test suite
- Build verification

### 4. Commit and Push

```bash
git add .
git commit -m "Add your feature"
git push origin feature/your-feature-name
```

### 5. Open a Pull Request

Open a PR against the `main` branch with:
- Clear description of changes
- Link to any related issues
- Screenshots if applicable

## Code Style

The project uses [Biome](https://biomejs.dev/) for linting and formatting:

```bash
# Check for issues
npm run check

# Auto-fix and format
npm run format
```

## Testing Guidelines

- Write tests for new functionality
- Test edge cases
- Use descriptive test names
- Keep tests focused and isolated

Example test structure:

```typescript
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';

describe('featureName', () => {
  it('should handle basic case', () => {
    // Arrange
    const input = 'test';

    // Act
    const result = yourFunction(input);

    // Assert
    expect(result).toBe('expected');
  });

  it('should handle edge case', () => {
    // ...
  });
});
```

## Building

The project bundles to a single file using `@vercel/ncc`:

```bash
npm run build
```

This creates `dist/index.js` which is the actual file executed by GitHub Actions.

**Important**: The `dist/` directory must be committed. CI will verify it's up to date.

# installation.mdx

Source: https://github.com/7nohe/confluence-md/blob/main/docs/src/content/docs/getting-started/installation.mdx

title: Installation
description: How to set up the Confluence MD GitHub Action in your repository.

## Prerequisites

Before using this action, you need:

1. A **Confluence Cloud** instance (e.g., `https://your-domain.atlassian.net`)
2. A Confluence account with **edit permissions** for the target page
3. An **API token** for authentication

## Creating an API Token

1. Go to [Atlassian API Tokens](https://id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens)
2. Click **Create API token**
3. Give it a descriptive name (e.g., "GitHub Actions")
4. Copy the token immediately (you won't be able to see it again)

## Setting Up GitHub Secrets

Add the following secrets to your repository:

1. Go to your repository's **Settings** > **Secrets and variables** > **Actions**
2. Add the following secrets:

| Secret Name | Description |
|-------------|-------------|
| `CONFLUENCE_EMAIL` | Your Confluence account email |
| `CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN` | The API token you created |

## Adding the Action to Your Workflow

Create a workflow file at `.github/workflows/confluence.yml`:

```yaml
name: Sync to Confluence

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'docs/**/*.md'

jobs:
  sync:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: daiki/confluence-md@v1
        with:
          confluence_base_url: https://your-domain.atlassian.net
          email: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_EMAIL }}
          api_token: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN }}
          source: docs/README.md
```

## Finding Your Page ID

The page ID can be found in the Confluence page URL:

```
https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SPACE/pages/123456789/Page+Title
                                                       ^^^^^^^^^
                                                       This is the page ID
```

You can specify the page ID either:
- In the workflow file using the `page_id` input
- In the Markdown file's frontmatter (recommended)

See [Quick Start](/getting-started/quick-start/) for frontmatter examples.

---

# My Documentation

Source: https://github.com/7nohe/confluence-md/blob/main/docs/src/content/docs/getting-started/quick-start.mdx

title: Quick Start
description: Get up and running with Confluence MD in 5 minutes.

This guide will help you sync your first Markdown file to Confluence.

## Step 1: Prepare Your Markdown File

Create a Markdown file with frontmatter containing the Confluence page ID:

```markdown
---
confluence_page_id: 123456789
---

# My Documentation

This content will be synced to Confluence.

## Features

- **Bold** and *italic* text
- Code blocks with syntax highlighting
- Tables and lists
```

## Step 2: Create the Workflow

Create `.github/workflows/confluence.yml`:

```yaml
name: Sync to Confluence

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'docs/**/*.md'

jobs:
  sync:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: daiki/confluence-md@v1
        with:
          confluence_base_url: ${{ vars.CONFLUENCE_BASE_URL }}
          email: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_EMAIL }}
          api_token: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN }}
          source: docs/README.md
```

## Step 3: Configure Secrets

Add the required secrets to your repository (see [Installation](/getting-started/installation/) for details).

## Step 4: Push and Verify

1. Commit and push your changes
2. Go to **Actions** tab to see the workflow run
3. Check your Confluence page for the updated content

## Using Action Outputs

The action provides useful outputs you can use in subsequent steps:

```yaml
- uses: daiki/confluence-md@v1
  id: confluence
  with:
    confluence_base_url: ${{ vars.CONFLUENCE_BASE_URL }}
    email: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_EMAIL }}
    api_token: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN }}
    source: docs/README.md

- name: Show Results
  run: |
    echo "Page URL: ${{ steps.confluence.outputs.page_url }}"
    echo "Updated: ${{ steps.confluence.outputs.updated }}"
    echo "Version: ${{ steps.confluence.outputs.version }}"
```

## Next Steps

- Learn about [Frontmatter options](/guides/frontmatter/)
- Understand [Image handling](/guides/images/)
- See all [Input parameters](/reference/inputs/)

# basic-usage.mdx

Source: https://github.com/7nohe/confluence-md/blob/main/docs/src/content/docs/guides/basic-usage.mdx

title: Basic Usage
description: Learn the fundamental patterns for using Confluence MD.

## Workflow Patterns

### Single File Sync

The simplest use case - sync one Markdown file to one Confluence page:

```yaml
- uses: daiki/confluence-md@v1
  with:
    confluence_base_url: https://your-domain.atlassian.net
    email: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_EMAIL }}
    api_token: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN }}
    source: docs/README.md
```

### Multiple Files

Use a matrix strategy to sync multiple files:

```yaml
jobs:
  sync:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        file:
          - docs/guide.md
          - docs/api.md
          - docs/faq.md
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: daiki/confluence-md@v1
        with:
          confluence_base_url: ${{ vars.CONFLUENCE_BASE_URL }}
          email: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_EMAIL }}
          api_token: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN }}
          source: ${{ matrix.file }}
```

### Conditional Sync

Only sync when specific files change:

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'docs/**/*.md'
```

## Dry Run Mode

Test your configuration without updating Confluence:

```yaml
- uses: daiki/confluence-md@v1
  with:
    confluence_base_url: ${{ vars.CONFLUENCE_BASE_URL }}
    email: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_EMAIL }}
    api_token: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN }}
    source: docs/README.md
    dry_run: 'true'
```

This generates the Confluence storage format and outputs without making any API calls to update the page.

## Skip Unchanged Content

By default, the action skips updates when content hasn't changed:

```yaml
- uses: daiki/confluence-md@v1
  with:
    # ... other inputs
    skip_if_unchanged: 'true'  # This is the default
```

The action computes a SHA256 hash of the generated content and compares it with the existing page. If they match, no update is performed.

## Overriding the Page Title

You can override the page title without modifying the Confluence page settings:

```yaml
- uses: daiki/confluence-md@v1
  with:
    # ... other inputs
    title_override: 'My Custom Title'
```

## Environment Variables vs Secrets

Use GitHub **variables** for non-sensitive data and **secrets** for sensitive data:

```yaml
- uses: daiki/confluence-md@v1
  with:
    confluence_base_url: ${{ vars.CONFLUENCE_BASE_URL }}  # Variable
    email: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_EMAIL }}                 # Secret
    api_token: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN }}         # Secret
    source: docs/README.md
```

---

# Your Content Here

Source: https://github.com/7nohe/confluence-md/blob/main/docs/src/content/docs/guides/frontmatter.mdx

title: Frontmatter
description: Configure Confluence page settings using YAML frontmatter in your Markdown files.

Frontmatter is YAML metadata at the beginning of your Markdown file, enclosed by `---` delimiters.

## Basic Frontmatter

The most common use is to specify the Confluence page ID:

```markdown
---
confluence_page_id: 123456789
---

# Your Content Here
```

## Custom Frontmatter Key

By default, the action looks for `confluence_page_id`. You can customize this:

```yaml
- uses: daiki/confluence-md@v1
  with:
    # ... other inputs
    frontmatter_page_id_key: 'page_id'
```

Then in your Markdown:

```markdown
---
page_id: 123456789
---
```

## Frontmatter vs Action Input

You can specify the page ID in two ways:

| Method | Priority | Use Case |
|--------|----------|----------|
| Frontmatter | Higher | When each Markdown file maps to a specific page |
| Action Input (`page_id`) | Lower (fallback) | When syncing multiple files to the same page |

Example with fallback:

```yaml
- uses: daiki/confluence-md@v1
  with:
    # ... other inputs
    page_id: '123456789'  # Used only if frontmatter is missing
    source: docs/README.md
```

## Multiple Metadata Fields

You can include other metadata in frontmatter - the action only reads the page ID key:

```markdown
---
title: My Documentation
author: John Doe
date: 2024-01-15
confluence_page_id: 123456789
tags:
  - documentation
  - api
---

# Content
```

## Finding Your Page ID

The page ID is visible in the Confluence URL:

```
https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SPACE/pages/123456789/Page+Title
```

You can also find it via the Confluence API or by clicking the page menu (**...**) and selecting **Page Information**.

---

# images.mdx

Source: https://github.com/7nohe/confluence-md/blob/main/docs/src/content/docs/guides/images.mdx

title: Image Handling
description: How to include images in your Markdown and have them appear in Confluence.

The action supports both local and remote images with flexible handling options.

## Local Images

Local images are resolved relative to your Markdown file or a custom base directory.

### Default Behavior

```markdown
![Screenshot](./images/screenshot.png)
```

By default, the image path is resolved relative to the Markdown file's directory.

### Custom Base Directory

Use `attachments_base` to specify a different base directory:

```yaml
- uses: daiki/confluence-md@v1
  with:
    # ... other inputs
    source: docs/guide.md
    attachments_base: 'assets/'
```

Now `![Logo](logo.png)` resolves to `assets/logo.png`.

## Image Modes

The `image_mode` input controls how images are handled:

### Upload Mode (Default)

```yaml
image_mode: 'upload'
```

- Local images are uploaded as Confluence page attachments
- Images appear as `<ac:image><ri:attachment ri:filename="..."/></ac:image>`
- Best for: Self-contained documentation, offline access

### External Mode

```yaml
image_mode: 'external'
```

- Images are referenced by URL
- Remote images remain as external links
- Local images still need to be accessible via URL
- Best for: When images are hosted elsewhere

## Remote Images

Remote images (starting with `http://` or `https://`) are handled based on your settings:

### Default (External Reference)

```markdown
![Diagram](https://example.com/diagram.png)
```

Renders as: `<ac:image><ri:url ri:value="https://example.com/diagram.png"/></ac:image>`

### Download and Upload

```yaml
download_remote_images: 'true'
```

Remote images are downloaded and uploaded as attachments. This:
- Makes your Confluence page self-contained
- Protects against external link rot
- May increase page load time during sync

## Duplicate Filenames

When multiple images have the same filename, the action adds numeric suffixes:

```
logo.png      -> logo.png
logo.png      -> logo_1.png
images/logo.png -> logo_2.png
```

## Security Considerations

- Path traversal is prevented - images must be within the `attachments_base` directory
- The action validates image paths before uploading
- Remote image downloads are subject to network timeouts

## Supported Formats

All image formats supported by Confluence work:
- PNG, JPG, JPEG, GIF
- SVG
- WebP (may have limited preview support)

---

# mermaid.mdx

Source: https://github.com/7nohe/confluence-md/blob/main/docs/src/content/docs/guides/mermaid.mdx

title: Mermaid Diagrams
description: Include Mermaid diagrams in your Markdown and render them in Confluence.

The action automatically converts Mermaid code blocks to Confluence's Mermaid macro.

## Requirements

Your Confluence instance must have the **Mermaid Diagrams** app installed. This is available in the Atlassian Marketplace.

## Basic Usage

Simply use a fenced code block with `mermaid` as the language:

````markdown
```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Start] --> B{Decision}
    B -->|Yes| C[Action 1]
    B -->|No| D[Action 2]
    C --> E[End]
    D --> E
```
````

This converts to:

```xml
<ac:structured-macro ac:name="mermaid">
  <ac:plain-text-body><![CDATA[graph TD
    A[Start] --> B{Decision}
    B -->|Yes| C[Action 1]
    B -->|No| D[Action 2]
    C --> E[End]
    D --> E]]></ac:plain-text-body>
</ac:structured-macro>
```

## Supported Diagram Types

All Mermaid diagram types are supported, including:

### Flowcharts

````markdown
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A --> B --> C
```
````

### Sequence Diagrams

````markdown
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    Alice->>Bob: Hello
    Bob-->>Alice: Hi!
```
````

### Class Diagrams

````markdown
```mermaid
classDiagram
    Animal <|-- Dog
    Animal <|-- Cat
```
````

### State Diagrams

````markdown
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Active
    Active --> Inactive
    Inactive --> [*]
```
````

### Gantt Charts

````markdown
```mermaid
gantt
    title Project Timeline
    section Phase 1
    Task 1: 2024-01-01, 30d
    Task 2: 2024-01-15, 20d
```
````

### Entity Relationship Diagrams

````markdown
```mermaid
erDiagram
    CUSTOMER ||--o{ ORDER : places
    ORDER ||--|{ LINE-ITEM : contains
```
````

## Troubleshooting

### Diagram Not Rendering

1. Verify the Mermaid app is installed in your Confluence instance
2. Check the diagram syntax using the [Mermaid Live Editor](https://mermaid.live/)
3. Ensure there are no extra spaces before the closing backticks

### Complex Diagrams

For very complex diagrams, consider:
- Breaking them into smaller diagrams
- Using the Mermaid app's native editor in Confluence for fine-tuning
- Testing the diagram in Mermaid Live Editor first

---

Source: https://github.com/7nohe/confluence-md/blob/main/docs/src/content/docs/index.mdx

title: Confluence MD

# architecture.mdx

Source: https://github.com/7nohe/confluence-md/blob/main/docs/src/content/docs/ja/development/architecture.mdx

title: アーキテクチャ
description: プロジェクト構造と実行フローの技術概要

## プロジェクト構造

```
confluence-md/
├── src/
│   ├── main.ts              # エントリーポイント、フローの調整
│   ├── types.ts             # TypeScriptインターフェース
│   ├── inputs.ts            # GitHub Action入力処理
│   ├── frontmatter.ts       # YAMLフロントマター抽出
│   ├── images.ts            # 画像パスユーティリティ
│   ├── converter/
│   │   ├── index.ts         # Unifiedプロセッサパイプライン
│   │   ├── nodes.ts         # ASTノードコンバーター
│   │   └── xml.ts           # XMLユーティリティ
│   └── confluence/
│       ├── client.ts        # HTTPクライアントラッパー
│       ├── pages.ts         # ページAPI操作
│       └── attachments.ts   # 添付ファイル処理
├── tests/                   # Vitestテストスイート
├── dist/                    # バンドル出力（ncc）
└── action.yml               # GitHub Actionメタデータ
```

## 実行フロー

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[入力を読み込み] --> B[Markdownファイルを読み込み]
    B --> C[フロントマターを抽出]
    C --> D[MarkdownをASTにパース]
    D --> E[ASTをConfluence XMLに変換]
    E --> F[コンテンツハッシュを計算]
    F --> G{ドライラン？}
    G -->|はい| H[結果を出力]
    G -->|いいえ| I[現在のページを取得]
    I --> J{コンテンツ変更？}
    J -->|いいえ| H
    J -->|はい| K[添付ファイルをアップロード]
    K --> L[ページを更新]
    L --> H
```

## 主要モジュール

### 入力処理 (`src/inputs.ts`)

GitHub Action入力を読み取り、検証します：
- ConfluenceベースURLを正規化（末尾のスラッシュを削除）
- オプション入力のデフォルト値を設定
- 必須入力が存在することを検証

### フロントマター (`src/frontmatter.ts`)

`gray-matter`を使用してYAMLフロントマターを抽出：
- フロントマターブロックをパース
- 設定されたキーを使用してページIDを抽出
- メタデータとコンテンツ本文の両方を返す

### コンバーター (`src/converter/`)

#### `index.ts`
unified処理パイプラインを作成：
```
remark-parse → remark-gfm → カスタムコンバーター → Confluence XML
```

後でアップロードするために変換中に見つかった画像を追跡します。

#### `nodes.ts`
再帰的ASTノードコンバーターが処理：
- ブロック要素（段落、見出し、リスト、テーブル）
- インライン要素（太字、斜体、コード、リンク）
- 特殊要素（コードブロック、画像、Mermaid）

#### `xml.ts`
XMLユーティリティ：
- `escapeXml()` - 特殊文字をエスケープ
- `cdata()` - コンテンツをCDATAセクションでラップ
- `el()` - XML要素を作成
- `macro()` - Confluenceマクロ要素を作成

### Confluenceクライアント (`src/confluence/`)

#### `client.ts`
`@actions/http-client`を使用したHTTPクライアントラッパー：
- Basic認証（email:token）
- JSONリクエスト/レスポンス処理
- 添付ファイル用マルチパートフォームデータ

#### `pages.ts`
Confluence v2 APIを使用したページ操作：
- `getPage()` - ストレージ本文付きでページを取得
- `updatePage()` - ページコンテンツとバージョンを更新

#### `attachments.ts`
Confluence v1 APIを使用した添付ファイル処理：
- `uploadAttachment()` - ファイルを添付ファイルとしてアップロード
- `downloadImage()` - リモート画像をダウンロード

## APIバージョン

Actionは異なるConfluence APIバージョンを使用：

| API | バージョン | エンドポイントパターン |
|-----|-----------|----------------------|
| ページ | v2 | `/wiki/api/v2/pages/{id}` |
| 添付ファイル | v1 | `/wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/child/attachment` |

v2 APIはよりクリーンなJSONレスポンスを提供するためページに使用。v1 APIは添付ファイルのアップロードがv2で利用できないため使用。

## コンテンツハッシュ

`skip_if_unchanged`を有効にするため、Actionは：
1. 生成されたストレージ形式のSHA256ハッシュを計算
2. 最初の16文字に切り詰め
3. ページプロパティに保存されたハッシュと比較（利用可能な場合）
4. ハッシュが一致する場合は更新をスキップ

## ビルドプロセス

プロジェクトは`@vercel/ncc`を使用してすべての依存関係を単一ファイルにバンドル：

```bash
npm run build  # dist/index.jsに出力
```

これにより、実行時に`node_modules`を必要としない自己完結型バンドルが作成されます。

---

# リポジトリをクローン

Source: https://github.com/7nohe/confluence-md/blob/main/docs/src/content/docs/ja/development/contributing.mdx

title: 開発への参加
description: Confluence MDプロジェクトへの貢献方法

## 開発環境のセットアップ

### 前提条件

- Node.js 20以上
- npm

### 開始

```bash
# リポジトリをクローン
git clone https://github.com/daiki/confluence-md.git
cd confluence-md

# 依存関係をインストール
npm install
```

## 利用可能なコマンド

| コマンド | 説明 |
|---------|------|
| `npm run build` | nccで`dist/index.js`にバンドル |
| `npm test` | 完全なテストスイートを実行 |
| `npm run test:watch` | ウォッチモードでテストを実行 |
| `npm run typecheck` | TypeScript型チェック |
| `npm run check` | Biomeリンティング |
| `npm run format` | Biomeでコードをフォーマット |
| `npm run ci` | すべてのチェックを実行（lint、typecheck、test、build） |

## テストの実行

```bash
# すべてのテストを実行
npm test

# 特定のテストファイルを実行
npx vitest run tests/converter.test.ts

# パターンに一致するテストを実行
npx vitest run -t "should convert h1"

# 開発用ウォッチモード
npm run test:watch
```

## プロジェクト構造

```
src/
├── main.ts           # エントリーポイント
├── types.ts          # TypeScriptインターフェース
├── inputs.ts         # 入力処理
├── frontmatter.ts    # フロントマター抽出
├── images.ts         # 画像ユーティリティ
├── converter/        # Markdown → Confluence変換
│   ├── index.ts
│   ├── nodes.ts
│   └── xml.ts
└── confluence/       # Confluence APIクライアント
    ├── client.ts
    ├── pages.ts
    └── attachments.ts
```

## 変更を加える

### 1. ブランチを作成

```bash
git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name
```

### 2. 変更を加える

- 既存のコードスタイルに従う
- 新機能にはテストを追加
- 必要に応じてドキュメントを更新

### 3. チェックを実行

```bash
npm run ci
```

これにより以下が実行されます：
- Biomeによるリンティング
- 型チェック
- テストスイート
- ビルド検証

### 4. コミットとプッシュ

```bash
git add .
git commit -m "機能を追加"
git push origin feature/your-feature-name
```

### 5. プルリクエストを開く

`main`ブランチに対してPRを開き、以下を含める：
- 変更の明確な説明
- 関連するIssueへのリンク
- 該当する場合はスクリーンショット

## コードスタイル

プロジェクトはリンティングとフォーマットに[Biome](https://biomejs.dev/)を使用：

```bash
# 問題をチェック
npm run check

# 自動修正とフォーマット
npm run format
```

## テストガイドライン

- 新機能にはテストを書く
- エッジケースをテスト
- 説明的なテスト名を使用
- テストは集中的で独立させる

テスト構造の例：

```typescript
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';

describe('機能名', () => {
  it('基本ケースを処理する', () => {
    // Arrange
    const input = 'test';

    // Act
    const result = yourFunction(input);

    // Assert
    expect(result).toBe('expected');
  });

  it('エッジケースを処理する', () => {
    // ...
  });
});
```

## ビルド

プロジェクトは`@vercel/ncc`を使用して単一ファイルにバンドル：

```bash
npm run build
```

これにより`dist/index.js`が作成され、これがGitHub Actionsで実際に実行されるファイルです。

**重要**: `dist/`ディレクトリはコミットする必要があります。CIは最新であることを検証します。

# installation.mdx

Source: https://github.com/7nohe/confluence-md/blob/main/docs/src/content/docs/ja/getting-started/installation.mdx

title: インストール
description: リポジトリにConfluence MD GitHub Actionをセットアップする方法

## 前提条件

このActionを使用する前に、以下が必要です：

1. **Confluence Cloud**インスタンス（例：`https://your-domain.atlassian.net`）
2. 対象ページの**編集権限**を持つConfluenceアカウント
3. 認証用の**APIトークン**

## APIトークンの作成

1. [Atlassian APIトークン](https://id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens)にアクセス
2. **APIトークンを作成**をクリック
3. わかりやすい名前を付ける（例：「GitHub Actions」）
4. トークンをすぐにコピー（再表示できません）

## GitHubシークレットの設定

リポジトリに以下のシークレットを追加します：

1. リポジトリの**Settings** > **Secrets and variables** > **Actions**に移動
2. 以下のシークレットを追加：

| シークレット名 | 説明 |
|---------------|------|
| `CONFLUENCE_EMAIL` | Confluenceアカウントのメールアドレス |
| `CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN` | 作成したAPIトークン |

## ワークフローへのActionの追加

`.github/workflows/confluence.yml`にワークフローファイルを作成：

```yaml
name: Confluenceに同期

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'docs/**/*.md'

jobs:
  sync:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: daiki/confluence-md@v1
        with:
          confluence_base_url: https://your-domain.atlassian.net
          email: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_EMAIL }}
          api_token: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN }}
          source: docs/README.md
```

## ページIDの確認方法

ページIDはConfluenceページのURLで確認できます：

```
https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SPACE/pages/123456789/Page+Title
                                                       ^^^^^^^^^
                                                       これがページID
```

ページIDは以下のいずれかで指定できます：
- ワークフローファイルの`page_id`入力
- Markdownファイルのフロントマター（推奨）

フロントマターの例は[クイックスタート](/ja/getting-started/quick-start/)を参照してください。

---

# ドキュメント

Source: https://github.com/7nohe/confluence-md/blob/main/docs/src/content/docs/ja/getting-started/quick-start.mdx

title: クイックスタート
description: 5分でConfluence MDを使い始める

このガイドでは、最初のMarkdownファイルをConfluenceに同期する方法を説明します。

## ステップ1: Markdownファイルを準備

ConfluenceページIDを含むフロントマター付きのMarkdownファイルを作成：

```markdown
---
confluence_page_id: 123456789
---

# ドキュメント

このコンテンツがConfluenceに同期されます。

## 機能

- **太字**と*斜体*テキスト
- シンタックスハイライト付きコードブロック
- テーブルとリスト
```

## ステップ2: ワークフローを作成

`.github/workflows/confluence.yml`を作成：

```yaml
name: Confluenceに同期

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'docs/**/*.md'

jobs:
  sync:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: daiki/confluence-md@v1
        with:
          confluence_base_url: ${{ vars.CONFLUENCE_BASE_URL }}
          email: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_EMAIL }}
          api_token: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN }}
          source: docs/README.md
```

## ステップ3: シークレットを設定

リポジトリに必要なシークレットを追加（詳細は[インストール](/ja/getting-started/installation/)を参照）。

## ステップ4: プッシュして確認

1. 変更をコミットしてプッシュ
2. **Actions**タブでワークフローの実行を確認
3. Confluenceページで更新されたコンテンツを確認

## Action出力の使用

Actionは後続のステップで使用できる出力を提供します：

```yaml
- uses: daiki/confluence-md@v1
  id: confluence
  with:
    confluence_base_url: ${{ vars.CONFLUENCE_BASE_URL }}
    email: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_EMAIL }}
    api_token: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN }}
    source: docs/README.md

- name: 結果を表示
  run: |
    echo "ページURL: ${{ steps.confluence.outputs.page_url }}"
    echo "更新済み: ${{ steps.confluence.outputs.updated }}"
    echo "バージョン: ${{ steps.confluence.outputs.version }}"
```

## 次のステップ

- [フロントマターオプション](/ja/guides/frontmatter/)を学ぶ
- [画像の扱い](/ja/guides/images/)を理解する
- すべての[入力パラメータ](/ja/reference/inputs/)を確認する

---

# basic-usage.mdx

Source: https://github.com/7nohe/confluence-md/blob/main/docs/src/content/docs/ja/guides/basic-usage.mdx

title: 基本的な使い方
description: Confluence MDの基本的な使用パターンを学ぶ

## ワークフローパターン

### 単一ファイルの同期

最もシンプルなユースケース - 1つのMarkdownファイルを1つのConfluenceページに同期：

```yaml
- uses: daiki/confluence-md@v1
  with:
    confluence_base_url: https://your-domain.atlassian.net
    email: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_EMAIL }}
    api_token: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN }}
    source: docs/README.md
```

### 複数ファイル

マトリックス戦略を使用して複数のファイルを同期：

```yaml
jobs:
  sync:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        file:
          - docs/guide.md
          - docs/api.md
          - docs/faq.md
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: daiki/confluence-md@v1
        with:
          confluence_base_url: ${{ vars.CONFLUENCE_BASE_URL }}
          email: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_EMAIL }}
          api_token: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN }}
          source: ${{ matrix.file }}
```

### 条件付き同期

特定のファイルが変更されたときのみ同期：

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'docs/**/*.md'
```

## ドライランモード

Confluenceを更新せずに設定をテスト：

```yaml
- uses: daiki/confluence-md@v1
  with:
    confluence_base_url: ${{ vars.CONFLUENCE_BASE_URL }}
    email: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_EMAIL }}
    api_token: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN }}
    source: docs/README.md
    dry_run: 'true'
```

Confluenceストレージ形式を生成し、出力しますが、ページを更新するAPIコールは行いません。

## 未変更コンテンツのスキップ

デフォルトでは、コンテンツが変更されていない場合は更新をスキップします：

```yaml
- uses: daiki/confluence-md@v1
  with:
    # ... その他の入力
    skip_if_unchanged: 'true'  # これがデフォルト
```

Actionは生成されたコンテンツのSHA256ハッシュを計算し、既存のページと比較します。一致する場合、更新は実行されません。

## ページタイトルの上書き

Confluenceページの設定を変更せずにページタイトルを上書きできます：

```yaml
- uses: daiki/confluence-md@v1
  with:
    # ... その他の入力
    title_override: 'カスタムタイトル'
```

## 環境変数 vs シークレット

非機密データにはGitHub **variables**を、機密データには**secrets**を使用：

```yaml
- uses: daiki/confluence-md@v1
  with:
    confluence_base_url: ${{ vars.CONFLUENCE_BASE_URL }}  # Variable
    email: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_EMAIL }}                 # Secret
    api_token: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN }}         # Secret
    source: docs/README.md
```

---

# コンテンツ

Source: https://github.com/7nohe/confluence-md/blob/main/docs/src/content/docs/ja/guides/frontmatter.mdx

title: フロントマター
description: Markdownファイルでフロントマターを使用してConfluenceページ設定を行う

フロントマターは、Markdownファイルの先頭にある`---`で囲まれたYAMLメタデータです。

## 基本的なフロントマター

最も一般的な使い方は、ConfluenceページIDの指定です：

```markdown
---
confluence_page_id: 123456789
---

# コンテンツ
```

## カスタムフロントマターキー

デフォルトでは`confluence_page_id`を探しますが、カスタマイズ可能です：

```yaml
- uses: daiki/confluence-md@v1
  with:
    # ... その他の入力
    frontmatter_page_id_key: 'page_id'
```

Markdownでは：

```markdown
---
page_id: 123456789
---
```

## フロントマター vs Action入力

ページIDは2つの方法で指定できます：

| 方法 | 優先度 | ユースケース |
|------|--------|-------------|
| フロントマター | 高い | 各MarkdownファイルをそれぞれのページにマッピングA場合 |
| Action入力（`page_id`） | 低い（フォールバック） | 複数ファイルを同じページに同期する場合 |

フォールバックの例：

```yaml
- uses: daiki/confluence-md@v1
  with:
    # ... その他の入力
    page_id: '123456789'  # フロントマターがない場合のみ使用
    source: docs/README.md
```

## 複数のメタデータフィールド

フロントマターには他のメタデータも含められます - ActionはページIDキーのみを読み取ります：

```markdown
---
title: ドキュメント
author: 山田太郎
date: 2024-01-15
confluence_page_id: 123456789
tags:
  - ドキュメント
  - api
---

# コンテンツ
```

## ページIDの確認方法

ページIDはConfluence URLで確認できます：

```
https://your-domain.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SPACE/pages/123456789/Page+Title
```

また、Confluence APIや、ページメニュー（**...**）から**ページ情報**を選択しても確認できます。

---

# images.mdx

Source: https://github.com/7nohe/confluence-md/blob/main/docs/src/content/docs/ja/guides/images.mdx

title: 画像の扱い
description: Markdownに画像を含め、Confluenceで表示する方法

Actionはローカルとリモートの両方の画像をサポートし、柔軟な処理オプションを提供します。

## ローカル画像

ローカル画像はMarkdownファイルのディレクトリまたはカスタムベースディレクトリからの相対パスで解決されます。

### デフォルトの動作

```markdown
![スクリーンショット](./images/screenshot.png)
```

デフォルトでは、画像パスはMarkdownファイルのディレクトリからの相対パスとして解決されます。

### カスタムベースディレクトリ

`attachments_base`を使用して別のベースディレクトリを指定：

```yaml
- uses: daiki/confluence-md@v1
  with:
    # ... その他の入力
    source: docs/guide.md
    attachments_base: 'assets/'
```

これで`![ロゴ](logo.png)`は`assets/logo.png`に解決されます。

## 画像モード

`image_mode`入力で画像の処理方法を制御します：

### アップロードモード（デフォルト）

```yaml
image_mode: 'upload'
```

- ローカル画像はConfluenceページの添付ファイルとしてアップロード
- 画像は`<ac:image><ri:attachment ri:filename="..."/></ac:image>`として表示
- 用途：自己完結型ドキュメント、オフラインアクセス

### 外部モード

```yaml
image_mode: 'external'
```

- 画像はURLで参照
- リモート画像は外部リンクのまま
- ローカル画像は別途URLでアクセス可能である必要あり
- 用途：画像が別の場所でホストされている場合

## リモート画像

リモート画像（`http://`または`https://`で始まる）は設定に応じて処理されます：

### デフォルト（外部参照）

```markdown
![図](https://example.com/diagram.png)
```

出力：`<ac:image><ri:url ri:value="https://example.com/diagram.png"/></ac:image>`

### ダウンロードしてアップロード

```yaml
download_remote_images: 'true'
```

リモート画像をダウンロードして添付ファイルとしてアップロードします。これにより：
- Confluenceページが自己完結型になる
- 外部リンク切れから保護
- 同期時のページ読み込み時間が増加する可能性

## ファイル名の重複

複数の画像が同じファイル名を持つ場合、Actionは数字のサフィックスを追加：

```
logo.png      -> logo.png
logo.png      -> logo_1.png
images/logo.png -> logo_2.png
```

## セキュリティ上の考慮事項

- パストラバーサルは防止されています - 画像は`attachments_base`ディレクトリ内にある必要があります
- Actionはアップロード前に画像パスを検証
- リモート画像のダウンロードはネットワークタイムアウトの対象

## サポートされる形式

Confluenceがサポートするすべての画像形式が動作します：
- PNG、JPG、JPEG、GIF
- SVG
- WebP（プレビューサポートが制限される場合あり）

---

# mermaid.mdx

Source: https://github.com/7nohe/confluence-md/blob/main/docs/src/content/docs/ja/guides/mermaid.mdx

title: Mermaidダイアグラム
description: MarkdownにMermaidダイアグラムを含め、Confluenceでレンダリングする

ActionはMermaidコードブロックをConfluenceのMermaidマクロに自動変換します。

## 必要条件

Confluenceインスタンスに**Mermaid Diagrams**アプリがインストールされている必要があります。これはAtlassian Marketplaceで入手できます。

## 基本的な使い方

言語として`mermaid`を指定したフェンスコードブロックを使用：

````markdown
```mermaid
graph TD
    A[開始] --> B{判断}
    B -->|はい| C[アクション1]
    B -->|いいえ| D[アクション2]
    C --> E[終了]
    D --> E
```
````

これは以下に変換されます：

```xml
<ac:structured-macro ac:name="mermaid">
  <ac:plain-text-body><![CDATA[graph TD
    A[開始] --> B{判断}
    B -->|はい| C[アクション1]
    B -->|いいえ| D[アクション2]
    C --> E[終了]
    D --> E]]></ac:plain-text-body>
</ac:structured-macro>
```

## サポートされる図の種類

すべてのMermaid図タイプがサポートされています：

### フローチャート

````markdown
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A --> B --> C
```
````

### シーケンス図

````markdown
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    アリス->>ボブ: こんにちは
    ボブ-->>アリス: やあ！
```
````

### クラス図

````markdown
```mermaid
classDiagram
    Animal <|-- Dog
    Animal <|-- Cat
```
````

### 状態図

````markdown
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> アクティブ
    アクティブ --> 非アクティブ
    非アクティブ --> [*]
```
````

### ガントチャート

````markdown
```mermaid
gantt
    title プロジェクトタイムライン
    section フェーズ1
    タスク1: 2024-01-01, 30d
    タスク2: 2024-01-15, 20d
```
````

### ER図

````markdown
```mermaid
erDiagram
    CUSTOMER ||--o{ ORDER : places
    ORDER ||--|{ LINE-ITEM : contains
```
````

## トラブルシューティング

### 図がレンダリングされない

1. ConfluenceインスタンスにMermaidアプリがインストールされているか確認
2. [Mermaid Live Editor](https://mermaid.live/)で図の構文を確認
3. 閉じバッククォートの前に余分なスペースがないか確認

### 複雑な図

非常に複雑な図の場合は、以下を検討：
- 小さな図に分割
- ConfluenceのMermaidアプリネイティブエディタで微調整
- まずMermaid Live Editorで図をテスト

# index.mdx

Source: https://github.com/7nohe/confluence-md/blob/main/docs/src/content/docs/ja/index.mdx

title: Confluence MD
description: MarkdownファイルをConfluence Cloudに変換し、ページを自動更新するGitHub Action
template: splash
hero:
  tagline: GitHub Actionひとつで、MarkdownドキュメントをConfluence Cloudに変換
  actions:
    - text: はじめる
      link: /ja/getting-started/installation/
      icon: right-arrow
    - text: GitHubで見る
      link: https://github.com/daiki/confluence-md
      icon: external
      variant: minimal

import { Card, CardGrid } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

## 機能

<CardGrid stagger>
  <Card title="GitHub Flavored Markdown" icon="document">
    テーブル、タスクリスト、取り消し線、コードブロックなどGFMを完全サポート。
  </Card>
  <Card title="Mermaidダイアグラム" icon="puzzle">
    MermaidコードブロックをConfluence Mermaidマクロに自動変換。
  </Card>
  <Card title="画像処理" icon="add-document">
    ローカル画像を添付ファイルとしてアップロード、または外部URLを使用。
  </Card>
  <Card title="スマート更新" icon="approve-check">
    コンテンツハッシュにより、変更がない場合は更新をスキップ。
  </Card>
</CardGrid>

## クイック例

```yaml
- uses: daiki/confluence-md@v1
  with:
    confluence_base_url: https://your-domain.atlassian.net
    email: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_EMAIL }}
    api_token: ${{ secrets.CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN }}
    source: docs/README.md
```
